title: C:ecology-with-reproduction attempt with a non-constructive E: a conserved catalysis-condensing enzyme (never made from food) lives as bands on c42's fuel-made prey droplets, eats them, divides with them, turns a frozen prey emulsion into a dividing one, and dissolves within 100 t when the prey are removed
summary: world.py keeps c42's closed food-chain prey (Cahn-Hilliard condensates made from fuel, decaying to waste, fuel regrown from waste) and replaces the predator condensate by an enzyme q that is conserved apart from a slow uniform turnover and is never made from prey: q drifts up its product r (catalysis-induced phase separation), and the catalysis kr c_a q^2 (1-r) that makes r consumes prey material (yield y2=0.03). From noise (seeds 0, 1; 128^2; t=12000; --lineage-k 5) about 30 consumer condensates form as rod-shaped bands on prey droplet edges and coexist with 35-50 prey to the end; labkit counts consumer persistent splits 29 and 31 (generation 2 and 4, merge/split 0.05) and prey persistent splits 74 and 79 (generation 6 and 8). Consumer bands divide when the prey droplet they eat into pinches (strips/s1_cons.png). Matched consumer-free twins (pred_on 0, same seeds, grid, duration, window) are frozen emulsions of 77 and 71 prey droplets with 7 and 2 persistent splits. Removing all prey material at t=3000 (efork_t3000) dissolves every consumer by t=3100 on both seeds (35 -> 0, 26 -> 0; max q 1.03 -> 0.08 = bath level) while the fed twins keep 25-37.

claims.statement: In pack/seed0 and pack/seed1 (world.py defaults, python -m labkit.run world.py --seeds <s> --frames 120 --lineage-k 5 --no-movie), consumer condensates of a conserved enzyme form from noise on fuel-made prey droplets; they persist as bands on prey edges, divide with the prey droplets they eat into (consumer persistent splits 29/31, generation 2/4), drive the prey from a frozen emulsion (twin) to a dividing population, and all dissolve within 100 t when the prey are removed while the fed twins keep theirs. The consumer is never made from its food: its dependence on prey is dynamical (its condensation needs the catalysis that eats prey).
claims.track: seed 1: the consumer band on the elongated prey droplet at t=6000 in strips/s1_cons.png row 2 divides with it into two consumer-prey pairs by t=6500; the same population (pack/seed1) is the fed twin of efork_t3000/seed1, where every consumer dissolves by t=3100 (efork.png)

controls_run.X: twin_nocons/seed0 and seed1 (pred_on 0, matched seeds, grid, duration and lineage window): 77 and 71 static prey, prey persistent splits 7 and 2 vs 74 and 79 with consumers; consumers lower the prey count (36 and 34 at the end vs 77 and 71)
controls_run.E: efork_t3000/seed0 and seed1 (prey material set to phi_a=-1 and prey production stopped at t=3000) vs the fed twins pack/seed0 and seed1 from the same seeds: consumers 35 -> 0 and 26 -> 0 by t=3100, max q returns to the bath 0.08 (efork.png, efork.json)

limits: Consumers are mostly bands lying on prey droplets, not free-swimming bodies; a few free consumer dots appear, but whether a consumer is an individual or a self-made layer of its prey is the main thing a reviewer should judge. Consumer division happens with prey pinching (joint division); a strict strip test (both daughters >= 8 px and present 5 frames = 500 t later; splits3.py) finds only 3 and 4 such events per seed against labkit's 29 and 31 persistent splits, so D for consumers rests on labkit's lineage and the strips. The prey are build-from-food (E by construction for prey, as in c42); the claimed E is the consumer's. The E fork removes all prey at once (no partial cut). dt=0.25 and dx=1 only; chiq >= 60 is numerically unstable at this dt. One parameter point (chiq 30, y2 0.03, na 1); y2 0.1 with na 2 (pack_na2_y01) gives coexistence but almost no persistent splits (0-2). No Laplacian-only twin.
